dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: The model uses only the official EF secondary data sets (plus a few approved proxies). The data set covers all materials over the supply chain of the represented cradle to gate inventory with a good overall data quality. The inventory is mainly based on Analysis of material efficiency aspects of Energy related Product for the development of EU Ecolabel criteria, European Commission. This data set is based on primary data from internationally adopted production processes, connected with regional precursor chains.

technology.technologicalApplicability: This data set is for fan for UPS

LCIMethodAndAllocation.deviationsFromLCIMethodApproaches: Background system: For the combined heat and power production, allocation by exergetic content is applied. For the electricity generation and by-products, e.g. gypsum, allocation by market value is applied due to no common physical properties. Within the refinery allocation by net calorific value and mass is used. For the combined crude oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids production allocation by net calorific value is applied. For details please see the document "GaBi Databases Modelling Principles"
LCIMethodAndAllocation.modellingConstants: Carbon storage and delayed emissions: credits associated with temporary (carbon) storage or delayed emissions are not considered. Emissions off-setting: not included. Capital goods are included, unless exclusion is justified along the overall 1% cut-off criterion. Direct land use change: GHG emissions from direct LUC allocated to good/service for 20 years after the LUC occurs. Fossil and biogenic carbon emissions and removals: removals and emissions are modelled as follows: All GHG emissions from fossil fuels (including peat and limestone) are modelled consistently with the ILCD list of elementary flows. In the case that the emissions refer to the molecules CO2 and CH4, they are modelled as ‘carbon dioxide (fossil)’ and ‘methane (fossil)’. Biogenic uptake and emissions are not modelled separately. For land use change, all carbon emissions and uptakes are inventoried separately for each of the elementary flows. Soil carbon accumulation (uptake) via improved agricultural management is excluded from the model.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataCutOffAndCompletenessPrinciples: cover at least 95% of environmental impacts
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataSelectionAndCombinationPrinciples: The model predominantly uses the mandatory EF data sets for both the foreground system and the background system, wherever available.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.useAdviceForDataSet: This LCI results data set is the (market) representative product of the fan, developed in context of the European Commission’s Environmental Footprint pilot phase 2013-2018. The datasets are specifically developed in compliance with the methodological requirements under the EF. The system boundary of this data set is cradle-to-gate.

common:scope.name: LCI results or Partly terminated system

review.common:reviewDetails: The data set achieves an overall DQR of 1.75, under the EF scheme of the PEFCR guidance 6.2. The foreground model is well representative of the depicted EU market of the reference flow, regarding both technological, geographical and time-related representativeness, while some relevant background data sets are less representative in these three aspects. The completeness of elementary flows of the 15 EF impact categories is “ good” for the foreground system and mostly “good” for some parts for the background system. The LCIA result of the data set per reference flow is plausible. The data set documentation is appropriate in scope and detail, and correctly reflects the model (judged with samples), including meeting the permissible cut-off rules, LCI modelling provisions and (fully checked) system boundaries. Based on expert judgement, the uncertainty of the data set is sufficiently limited. The names, classes/categories of newly created flows and processes are ILCD compliant, otherwise exclusively the eligible ILCD reference elementary flows, flow properties and unit groups are being used, including the regionalisation of the large majority of the water and land use flow amounts.
